① The headline question: is the arc wall the right path against quest sprawl?

Fable adjudication · #231, #229, #230 · owner ruling 2026-08-24

Verdict: right rail, incomplete wall. Keep the design — and close three holes before trusting it.

The diagnosis behind #231 is genuinely rigorous. Two intuitive explanations were measured and falsified on the t2324 save (duration — the favourite quest ran 161 turns; epistemic-vs-terminal goals — zero-box rates were flat), and the confirmed axis was proportion through anchoring: the giants thread at 7 quests was healthy precisely because it died with its arc, while the closed-eye thread hit 18 quests across ~8 arc boundaries because nothing tied it to anything. The wall enforces exactly the confirmed axis — an emergent thread is subordinated to the spine unit that bore it. Stamping at quest creation is the only deterministic join point (acceptance may never come; objectives may never be tagged). And the hard-wall-with-no-promotion ruling holds up better than it first looks: resurrection through a fresh |offered is player-gated — the reopen guard converts unbounded GM momentum into per-arc player consent, which is the agency mechanism the "player never gets a voice" worry asks for. The design panel that probed alternatives (promotion ceremony, proportional budget, player-facing choice at the wall) concluded the same: nothing on that list beats the shipped shape on the evidence available, and building promotion machinery now would be speculation ahead of data.

But as shipped, the wall would have only partially caught the campaign that motivated it. Three holes, in order:

1. Parallel acts are the wall's blind habitat (P0 item). When two or more arcs are live, currentArcTitle() returns null and nothing is stamped — deliberately, to avoid guessing. But the owner's own Runelords campaign spent ~45% of its turns (t878–t1922) inside a parallel act, and that stretch is where the sprawl lived. Everything born there is permanently immune. The fix that preserves the no-guessing principle: when the arc is ambiguous but the ACT is not, stamp the act (bornAct) and sweep at act completion.

2. ACT_COMPLETE is an open door (P0 item). Closing an act while one of its arcs is still active orphans that arc's progeny into permanent immunity — the act-level exit reintroduces exactly the sprawl the arc-level wall kills. These two fixes are one design.

3. The wall is blind after it fires (P0 item). Post-sweep, the crisis line still demands the GM register any pursued goal, the blocked |active re-creation is silent to the GM, and no note says the thread was closed — so the GM population the wall targets lands in an untracked-thread state, the exact green-indicators blindness #231 exists to end. A wall-variant 2-turn note (not the #229 "abandoned by the player" wording, which would be false) closes the loop.

What NOT to build yet: thread fingerprinting. The measured pathology was a thread of 18 retitled rows, and the wall polices rows — a well-behaved hydra that closes each row inside its arc never trips it (P1 item). That is a real granularity gap, but detecting "the same thread under new titles" is heavy, fuzzy machinery, and the honest move is the one the TODO row already names: gate it on the first armed campaign's field data. That measurement is currently impossible — wall-abandons and player-abandons write identical archive records — so the tiny by field (P2/P2) is not cosmetics, it is the instrument the next design decision depends on. Land it now.

The rest of the family: the same-response newborn-quest kill (P1), the Suggest-completion blast radius that can now fire the sweep from a utility click (P1, folds into the review-call whitelist P1), the resurrected-quest objective wipe (P1), and the small records in P2/P3. 11 items

Live canon-corruption and silent-recall-loss mechanisms, plus the three hardenings that make the arc wall actually cover the campaign shape that motivated it. Every one is drift-surface: Fable-tier builds.

  • ACT_COMPLETE is an open door in the wall — still-active arcs' progeny become permanently unsweepable
    highdrifteffort: mediumcertainverified: confirmed + confirmed arc-wall-impl

    If the GM closes an act while one of its arcs is still open, every side quest born under that arc escapes the wall forever — the exact sprawl the feature was built to kill comes back through the act-level exit.

    tag_table.js api.js
    Mechanism, remedy & verification record

    Mechanism

    tag_table.js:938-955 — the ACT_COMPLETE handler sets the act to "completed" and activates the next act's arcs, but never marks the closing act's still-active arcs completed and never runs the #231 sweep (the sweep lives only inside ARC_COMPLETE, tag_table.js:887-910). After the act closes, [ARC_COMPLETE:oldArc] can never fire for those arcs because the handler skips non-active acts (tag_table.js:880 `if(_sk.acts[_si].status!=="active")continue;`) — it warns "matches no ACTIVE arc — ignored" (line 916). So every quest stamped bornArc=<that arc> stays live forever: the sweep's match (line 897) requires the arc title to pass through an ARC_COMPLETE that is now unreachable. Nothing gates ACT_COMPLETE on all-arcs-done — the pacing doc (api.js:1841) says "When the act's turning point occurs, emit [ACT_COMPLETE:title]", and the F3 nudge (api.js:1848-1849) only encourages the tag, never withholds it. Model neglect of paired skeleton emissions is documented in this codebase (the F3 finding itself: acts sat active 4 turns after their last arc closed — the mirror-image neglect). Parallel acts make it worse: once a parallel act is down to ONE live arc, currentArcTitle (helpers.js:371-379) resumes stamping, and an early act-close then orphans that arc's progeny. The failure is silent — no warn, no census, and the orphans are indistinguishable from deliberately-immune legacy quests.

    Remedy

    Make ACT_COMPLETE finish its own act: mark the closing act's still-active arcs completed and run the same progeny sweep for each (extract the sweep body from the ARC_COMPLETE handler into a shared function both handlers call), with a failing-test-first asserting an [ACT_COMPLETE:] over a still-active arc archives that arc's stamped progeny as abandoned. Drift surface — Fable-tier per the decree.

    Fable adjudication

    Fable: fix alongside the parallel-act hole (the P0 item below) — both are exits from the same wall, and an act-level fallback stamp only works if ACT_COMPLETE also sweeps.

    Verifier corrections

    Two overstatements, neither load-bearing: (a) orphaned quests are NOT literally indistinguishable from legacy quests in data — they carry a bornArc stamp pointing at an arc inside a completed act, while legacy rows have no stamp; the accurate claim is that no runtime surface ever inspects bornArc against act status, so nothing flags them. (b) 'permanently unsweepable' is true of the automatic #231 wall only — the #191 quest-staleness nudge (ACTIVE quests, 30-turn clock; OFFERED orphans uncovered) and a manual GM [QUEST:title|completed/failed] can still close an orphan, though these are exactly the discretionary mechanisms whose documented field failure motivated #231. One strengthening fact the finding missed: ACT_COMPLETE never validates its title operand against the act (unlike ARC_COMPLETE post-#136①) — any [ACT_COMPLETE:anything] closes the current active act, widening the erroneous-early-close path.

    Minor: "orphans are indistinguishable from deliberately-immune legacy quests" is overstated — orphaned quests DO carry a bornArc stamp (pointing at an arc frozen "active" inside a completed act) while legacy/unstamped quests carry none, so a census could distinguish them; the claim holds only operationally, because no census or repair tool reads bornArc today. Also worth adding: the paired same-response emission [ARC_COMPLETE:x][ACT_COMPLETE:y] works correctly (ARC_COMPLETE precedes ACT_COMPLETE in table order — engine-tests.js:5256), so the leak is specifically the unpaired ACT_COMPLETE; and the act-budget pacing nudge (api.js:1868-1869) actively pushes the GM toward "the act's turning point" while an arc is still live, increasing the odds of exactly that unpaired emission.

  • Parallel-act immunity leaves the wall inert across the campaign phase where the measured sprawl lived

    In a parallel act the wall stamps nothing at all, and in the owner's own campaign the parallel act covered nearly half of all play — exactly the stretch where the runaway thread grew — so the shipped fix would have mostly sat idle in the very campaign that motivated it.

    helpers.js tag_table.js testRuns/Rise_of_the_Runelords__Ammut__Ammut_t2097.tnd
    Mechanism, remedy & verification record

    Mechanism

    helpers.js:371-379: currentArcTitle() returns null whenever the active act has more than one live arc (live.length===1 gate), so tag_table.js:582's creation stamp writes no bornArc for any quest born under a parallel act, and tag_table.js:897's sweep can never touch them. Real data: the t2097 save (same campaign the t2324 measurement came from) shows Act 1 'The Fall of the Runelord' is PARALLEL with all four arcs started at t878 and the next act starting t1922 — 1,044 turns, ~45% of the campaign, containing most of the closed-eye-family closes (The Spire's Reckoning t1491, Whispers from the Kodars t1525, The Spire's Bench t1857, the Justice Court cluster t1714-t1904). The 'ambiguous parent would sweep innocents' rationale is correct at ARC granularity but does not apply at ACT granularity — the bearing act is unambiguous.

    Remedy

    When currentArcTitle() is null but exactly one act is active, stamp bornAct instead, and have the ACT_COMPLETE handler run the same sweep over bornAct progeny (with the same runway note keyed to ACT_TURN_BUDGET). Coarser wall, same subordination principle, closes the largest coverage hole without guessing a parent.

    Fable adjudication

    Fable adjudication: this is the single most important hardening. The fix is to scope the stamp to the ACT when the arc is ambiguous (bornAct fallback), swept at ACT_COMPLETE — which requires closing the ACT_COMPLETE door in the same design.

    Verifier corrections

    The summary slightly overstates the counterfactual: the shipped wall would not have been fully idle in the motivating campaign. The closed-eye root began in Act 0's sequential Skinsaw arc and would have been stamped and swept at ~t878 when 'The Skinsaw Man' completed, and Act 2 births (t1922+) are covered (sweep at 'The Road to Xin-Shalast''s completion, t1977).   • Page-hide/unload sync flush silently fails on any mature campaign (64KB keepalive body limit)
    highrecalleffort: mediumcertainverified: confirmed + confirmed state-sync-perf

    The 'final turn always reaches the cloud when you close or background the game' guarantee is broken for every campaign past the first ~30 turns, and the failure is completely silent — which can later cost real turns when a second device overwrites the stale server copy.

    storage-adapter.js ui-boot.js
    Mechanism, remedy & verification record

    Mechanism

    ui-boot.js:277-278 wires beforeunload and visibilitychange(hidden) to storageAdapter.syncNow(true). The beacon path (storage-adapter.js:460-477) POSTs the FULL payload — compressed transcript + memory + sessionLog, proven multi-MB by the project's own 2MB sentinel firing at t1130 (storage-adapter.js:448-458) — via fetch(..., keepalive:true). The Fetch spec caps total in-flight keepalive request bodies at 64 KiB; Chrome/Safari reject the fetch with a network error the moment the body exceeds it. The rejection lands in .catch(function(){}) at storage-adapter.js:475 inside try{} at 466 — _onSyncFail is never called, the sync badge never turns red, no console line. Cascade: the unsynced final turn(s) stay local-only; if the player then plays on a second device, that device's higher server turn makes the first device's next reconcile ADOPT wholesale (storage-adapter.js:649-675, worldState = data.worldState), discarding the unflushed turns. Same-device recovery exists (visible-again re-sync at storage-adapter.js:889-893), so the loss path is specifically cross-device. CLAUDE.md §16 documents the guarantee as if it holds.

    Remedy

    In _syncNow's beacon branch, check payload.length against ~60KB: over the limit, fall back to a plain (non-keepalive) fetch — during visibilitychange(hidden) the page is still alive and the request usually completes — and in all cases route the rejection through _onSyncFail so the failure is loud. Longer term, a tiny keepalive-sized 'turn N is unsynced' marker POST would at least let the server/other devices detect staleness.

    Verifier corrections

    The "~30 turns" threshold is an unmeasured estimate, not a derived number — the payload ships LZ-compressed (#92, line 429), so the exact turn at which it crosses 64 KiB varies; the qualitative claim (any mature campaign is far past the limit) stands. Also, silent wholesale loss requires the second device to advance PAST the first device's local turn; if it does not, the first device instead lands in the loud CAS 409 conflict path (485-494) rather than silent adoption — still a consequence of the silent flush failure, but a different (visible) failure surface.

    Three detail fixes, all making the finding stronger or more precise: (1) the "~30 turns" onset is too generous — _stripNpcPortraits (storage-adapter.js:404-410) strips only NPC portraits; the PC's base64 portrait rides inline by design (396-401) and companion charSheet portraits ride unstripped, so a typical 40-100KB portrait data URL pushes the payload over 64KiB from nearly turn 1 for any character with a portrait. (2) The t1130 2MB sentinel firing predates the #92 transcript compression (the comment at 424-428 says compression was the response to it) — post-#92 payloads are smaller than multi-MB but still far above 64KiB. (3) "Completely silent" is slightly overstated on the same device: _syncOk is never called, so the persistent unsynced counter in syncStatus() does reflect the un-acked turns if the user later looks at the badge — but no failure surfacing (_onSyncFail) ever occurs, which is the load-bearing silent-failure claim (and violates the project's own no-silent-failures policy).

⑥ Dimension health — what is verified sound

the other half of the review: confirmations, not just defects

Each reviewer was required to state what it verified SOUND, not only what it found broken. These verdicts are the standing health record for each system as of v1.714.

arc-wall-impl · 7 findings

The wall's core design is sound and well-guarded: the emergent/spine predicate is single-sourced, the three pinned narrownesses (spine never stamped, unstamped immune, parallel stamps nothing) are real and sabotage-proven against the live code, the warn latch is correctly registered in NOTE_LATCH_FIELDS, and the sweep is loud at the moment it fires. The genuine defects are at boundaries the arc-level design didn't cover: [ACT_COMPLETE:] closes an act without completing or sweeping its still-active arcs, permanently orphaning their stamped progeny into exactly the sprawl the wall exists to kill; and table order stamps a same-response newborn quest with the dying arc and kills it at birth. On the entry's judgement calls: a `by` field is wanted (the reopen guard currently tells the GM a wall-swept quest was "abandoned by the player"); the no-runway-for-fast-arcs arithmetic is acceptable because the sweep itself is loud, but should be recorded as deliberate; and the [ARC_CONTINUE:] dodge is not worth new machinery — #127 escalation plus the warn note's "do NOT open further side threads" clause bound growth during an overstay, and the wall still falls whenever the arc finally closes.

quest-sprawl-design · 8 findings

The rail FAMILY is right and the owner should keep it: the falsification work (duration and epistemic-vs-terminal measured and rejected; proportion confirmed) is genuinely rigorous for n=1, subordinating emergent threads to authored spine units is the correct answer to a proportion violation, stamping at CREATION is the only deterministic join point (acceptance may never come, objectives may never be tagged), the three fail-safes are real and sabotage-pinned, and — contra the "player never gets a voice" worry — the abandoned-status reopen guard makes resurrection player-gated (fresh |offered, player accepts or declines), which converts unbounded GM momentum into per-arc player consent; that ceremony is the design's real agency mechanism and it is sound in principle. But as shipped the wall would have only partially caught the campaign that motivated it: the t2097 save shows the Runelords blueprint's middle act is PARALLEL and spans ~45% of the campaign (t878–t1922, the sprawl's habitat), where currentArcTitle returns null and nothing is ever stamped; and the wall polices quest ROWS while the measured pathology was a THREAD of 18 retitled rows, most of which would close inside their arcs and never touch it. The re-offer ceremony is also under-built — the wall arms no post-sweep prompt channel while buildQuestBlock's crisis line actively demands re-registration and the blocked |active recreation is silent to the GM — so the exact GM population the wall targets lands in an untracked-thread state, the blindness class #231 exists to end. Verdict: right path, incomplete rail — harden the parallel-act hole (scope to the ACT) and the post-sweep channel now; gate thread-fingerprinting and any promotion mechanism on the first armed campaign's data, which requires the `by` field so wall-abandons are countable at all.

Runelords Haiku playtest (v1.230)

Half-Infernal Half-Blood Sorcerer, Level 8
Turns 0–150 · 301 passages
Turn 0

The Swallowtail Festival banners are burning.

You smell it first, not the sharp bite of pine or torch-flame, but something richer, older. Ash drifts through Sandpoint's central square like snow in reverse, rising instead of falling. The cathedral's new bell tolls once, wrong, as if someone is ringing it in panic. Around you, townsfolk have stopped mid-celebration. A child's wooden toy lies abandoned in the dirt. The festival bonfire has grown teeth.

Victor Marlow stands at your shoulder, dark eyes already tracking movement at the square's far edge, the glint of crude spears catching firelight. His hand has found the pommel of one short blade without thinking. "Goblins," he says quietly. "More than a few." Peet raises one hand and whispers something ancient and wet. The ground beneath a cluster of goblins ripples. Skeletal arms erupt from the dirt, bone-white and wrong, seizing two of them and slamming them prone.

You step forward. Your dark glass rod hums in your grip, a subsonic frequency only you truly feel, warm as blood. The nearest goblin shrieks something in its own language, a sound like a kettle boiling dry. You don't bother with magic. The rod swings. His ribs cave inward. He doesn't get back up.

The townsfolk are running now, toward the cathedral. Good. A merchant woman pulls three children behind her. An old fisherman grabs a burning brand from the bonfire and waves it at the goblins, more courage than sense, but it works. They flinch.

Victor has already gutted one. His blade moves like it's apologizing to the goblin for how fast it's happening. Two more converge on him, crude swords raised.

How do you press the advantage?

I cut down the goblin raiders threatening Father Zantus at the podium, holding the line until the square is clear.

You don't let him. A side sweep takes his legs out from under him, and he tumbles backward down the stone. The third one actually manages to swing at you, a crude curved blade that catches your arm. Scope and standard

Complete editorial read, paper walkthroughs of alternative choices, and a real designer load/export check. This is not a completed gameplay or balance playtest. Findings are included only where a change has a concrete benefit for the player; stylistic substitutions alone are omitted. Suggested text is a proposal and has not been applied to the blueprint.

Author-facing review: plot revelations and endings are discussed throughout. Source fields below use zero-based JSON indexes.

The assessment

The box is valuable to three parties for three different reasons, and the company’s need to cross the Flats supplies immediate pressure. Hask’s ignorance is especially useful leverage. The campaign needs firmer custody, bargaining and travel rules so its final choice grows from decisions the player made rather than from a collision the outline requires.

What to preserve

Keep Hask mistaken rather than omniscientHis belief that he is seeking royal bones can be challenged with evidence. That creates a real reason to negotiate with a dangerous person.

Keep a genuine upside in every bargainThe rule that the God must honor a real benefit prevents the familiar “all deals are fake” trap. Pair that upside with discoverable limits.

Keep Corr and Ren vulnerable for different reasonsCorr’s illness and Ren’s fading memories can strain loyalty without making both secretly evil. Their needs should create choices, not compulsory betrayal.

Improvements worth making

High: resolve before relying on the affected scene in a player-facing playtest. Medium: a concrete improvement to clarity, agency or payoff. These are editorial priorities, not measured gameplay failure rates.

  1. Give the reliquary a clear custody chain and opening condition
  2. Make a successful intervention stop the cult’s awakening rite
  3. Make sorcery’s extra cost visible before a player commits
  4. Clarify the player’s authority over the Red Ledger
  5. Give the hundred-mile crossing a few concrete resource choices
  6. Bound the God’s promises and write the consequences of each custody decision
High priority · 1 of 6

Give the reliquary a clear custody chain and opening condition

Why this improves play

The key has no assigned carrier, the theft has no defined route into the hiring scene, and resealing has no specified requirements. The player cannot make an informed early decision to inspect, secure, abandon or open the cargo when its basic handling rules are left to the moment.

Source evidence · 3 excerpts
premise“bargain with anyone carrying the key”
npcs[0].notes“she stole it from a rival consul's tomb”
acts[2].turningPoint“reseal the Coffered God”
Recommended change

Write a short chain of custody: where Ysbet stole the box, why it is now at Kalgra’s Rest, who holds the key, and which vault is the actual destination. Distinguish the mundane lock from the magical seal. Seed the resealing method in Ren’s knowledge and a second existing source.

Suggested wording or scene · proposal, not existing canon

Proposed custody note: Ysbet stole the reliquary from her rival’s frontier tomb and routed it through Kalgra’s Rest to disguise its return into her own vault. Corr carries the outer lock’s key; opening that lock exposes the seal but does not release the entity. Ren can explain how to renew the salt binding, and Sister Ash-Tongue’s stolen sealing text supplies an independent account.

How to verify the improvement

Before leaving Kalgra’s Rest, the player should know what they can physically do to the box. Before the final choice, they should know what resealing requires and where to obtain it.

High priority · 2 of 6

Make a successful intervention stop the cult’s awakening rite

Why this improves play

The investigation invites the player to find cult infiltrators, yet the turning point requires their rite to happen anyway. The final gates also assume both forces converge even if the party has neutralized one faction. These fixed events can erase the point of successful planning.

Source evidence · 3 excerpts
acts[1].turningPoint“The Cinder Chorus performs a rite that partially wakes the Coffered God”
acts[1].arcs[1].objective“Investigate the cult's presence among the company's own hired hands”
acts[2].arcs[0].objective“the converged forces of Hask Vane and the Cinder Chorus”
Recommended change

Write conditional turning points. If the rite is prevented, the God remains less able to project and the cult must use a different, weaker approach. If Hask withdraws or joins the company, remove his hostile gate encounter and show the consequences of that agreement.

Suggested wording or scene · proposal, not existing canon

Proposed transition: an unopposed rite lets the God speak into the company’s dreams. If the party stops the rite, it can speak only through the established crack or a willing key-holder, and Ash-Tongue reaches Two Thrones without the intended following. The finale uses only forces that actually survived and remained hostile.

How to verify the improvement

Expose the cult before its rite and persuade Hask that the box is not royal bones. The final confrontation must be materially easier or different because both successes mattered.

High priority · 3 of 6

Make sorcery’s extra cost visible before a player commits

Why this improves play

This rule applies to every use of magic, not just the box or Ren’s practices. A character created with ordinary spells can unexpectedly lose memories or lifespan for using an established ability. Ren’s thematic cost is specific; the universal rule has no amount, choice or limit.

Source evidence · 3 excerpts
rules[0]“always extracts a cost paid in the caster's body, memory, or years”
rules[0]“whenever magic is used”
npcs[5].notes“a cost paid in her own memories”
Recommended change

Decide explicitly whether this is a campaign-wide change to character magic or a property of the setting’s extraordinary rites. My recommendation is to preserve established spell costs and put bodily, memory or lifespan bargains on named rituals whose price is revealed before consent. If universal costly magic is essential, disclose it at the opening and define the costs before the first cast.

Suggested wording or scene · proposal, not existing canon

Proposed rule: spells and abilities retain their established game costs. Sorcery involving the reliquary, Ren’s divinations or a new bargain may demand an additional named price. Explain that price before the character chooses; ordinary casting never silently consumes years or a personal memory.

How to verify the improvement

Try healing an injured companion in the first ambush. The result must use a cost the player could know before pressing the action, rather than an improvised permanent penalty.

Medium priority · 4 of 6

Clarify the player’s authority over the Red Ledger

Why this improves play

The player is expected to manage the company, while the commander is not identified and the starting relationship is unspecified. A solo protagonist may be treated as commander in one scene and as a disposable hire with no voice in the next.

Source evidence · 3 excerpts
npcs[3].notes“The Red Ledger's second-in-command”
acts[1].arcs[3].objective“Manage the company's internal loyalties”
premise“The company must decide whether they are guards, thieves, or unwitting midwives”
Recommended change

State the starting role and the company’s decision process. A useful default is a newly appointed field leader with Corr as the experienced deputy, while retaining an alternate role for a player who wants to be a hired specialist. Make companions’ reasons to follow or refuse explicit.

Suggested wording or scene · proposal, not existing canon

Proposed opening agreement: the player is contracted to lead this crossing, not to own its members. Corr handles routines and can challenge a plan that endangers the company. Major choices about the box are argued openly; dissent may split the company, but no absent commander can silently overrule an earned agreement.

How to verify the improvement

Ask who can order a route change, who decides whether to open the box, and what happens if Corr disagrees. Answer consistently for the chosen player role.

Medium priority · 5 of 6

Give the hundred-mile crossing a few concrete resource choices

Why this improves play

The environment promises that water and route choice matter, but the outline gives neither a travel schedule nor meaningful alternatives. Repeated thirst narration can become a punishment the GM applies whenever tension falls, while Ren becomes an unlimited or arbitrarily costly refill.

Source evidence · 3 excerpts
premise“a hundred miles of salt where water is currency and shade is a weapon”
locations[2].description“hidden cisterns make them both a refuge and an ambush ground”
npcs[5].notes“magic lets her read weather and water”
Recommended change

Define a compact itinerary with known replenishment points, carrying limits appropriate to the company, and a few announced choices. Use existing inventory and travel accounting where available; do not add a new hidden counter for every scene. Give Ren’s divination a fixed kind of question and an explicit price.

Suggested wording or scene · proposal, not existing canon

Proposed route choice: the exposed direct road is shorter but consumes the company’s reserve; the canyons offer a known cistern and ambush risk; a diversion to Ren’s cistern-house costs time and yields sealing knowledge. State the expected travel time and water consequence before the company chooses.

How to verify the improvement

Walk the crossing twice using different routes. Supplies, allies or arrival conditions should differ for traceable reasons, with no unannounced double-charge for the same travel.

High priority · 6 of 6

Bound the God’s promises and write the consequences of each custody decision

Why this improves play

Its ultimate nature can remain uncertain, but a bargain is unfair if its powers and price change to fit the player’s latest theory. “Reseal, deliver or open” is a strong menu of decisions only when their practical effects are seeded. There is no stated outcome for handing it over early or walking away.

Source evidence · 3 excerpts
npcs[4].notes“the GM should let players' theories shape how it manifests”
rules[1]“a real, honored upside alongside the hidden cost”
acts[2].turningPoint“deliver it to whichever faction the company has thrown in with, or break it open themselves”
Recommended change

Keep its ontology ambiguous while fixing a small set of powers, constraints and examples of costs. Give the player ways to investigate a bargain before accepting. Add aftermaths for resealing, giving it to Hask, helping the Chorus, opening it independently and abandoning the contract. Early decisions should move the ending, not force a replacement escort job.

Suggested wording or scene · proposal, not existing canon

Proposed boundary: the God can restore Corr’s health but claims a defined future service, not an unspecified additional life. It cannot possess an unwilling person merely because they listened. Resealing limits its reach; delivering it gives the named recipient control of a real danger; opening it changes the Flats in a consequence demonstrated by a smaller prior manifestation. Record one unsettled bargain per person and close it when paid.

How to verify the improvement

Offer the same bargain to two skeptical players, allow them to investigate separately, and keep the promise and price consistent. Then resolve an early handover without undoing it.

Sword and sorcery. A mercenary company escorts a sealed reliquary across a salt waste, hunted by a warlord, a cult, and the thing in the box that wants out.

Keep the current pitch. It accurately presents the crossing, the competing pursuers and the cargo’s dangerous agency. The God’s desire to escape is the central premise, not a late mystery that needs concealing.

Traffic and Dragons is a sword & sorcery role-playing game that runs entirely in your browser. You create a character, and an AI Game Master narrates a living adventure around you — tracking your health, gold, inventory, quests, and the people you meet, across sessions. There's nothing to install and no account for the game itself; the one thing you must bring is an Anthropic API key, which is what powers the Game Master's brain.
• Sheet (top bar) shows your full character — health, gold, inventory, spells, skills, relationships. It updates itself as you play.
<figcaption>The same panel ④ expanded — party health at a glance; Quests, Inventory, Abilities, and Spells one tap away.</figcaption>
SheetYour full character sheet — stats, portrait, abilities, spells, inventory, skills, relationships, story beats. Everything the game knows about you.
SyncThe "fix it yourself" hatch: directly edit HP, gold, inventory, time, weather and more — handy if the story and the numbers ever disagree.

The right edge of the screen. Collapsed, it's a slim rail of tabs (Pty · Qst · Inv · Ab · Sp); tap to expand it into full drawers — your Party with everyone's health bars, plus Quests, Inventory, Abilities, and Spells. Everything you'd flip to your character sheet for mid-scene, one tap away.
• A player may leave an item in their quarters and it must stay there until they retrieve it. A robust location-based inventory retention system is required.
• Places where a player can empty their inventory and spend gold. Items a player SELLS at a shop last the session but are not granted permanence (unlike items left in a house).

A. The riskless economy is the one place this lens objects on its own terms. Positions: 3.1 ● (scarcity; Monty Haul is a named failure mode), 2.3 ● (treasure's worth scales with the risk taken to win it), 7.3 ● (not a simulation). The proposal makes the village the sole place with a blacksmith, trading post, alchemist and healer, explicitly "where a player can empty their inventory and spend gold," with no dangers. Every acquisition in the village is bought, never won. For the player, the shape is: adventure earns gold under threat; the village converts gold to capability at zero threat, indefinitely, because the campaign never ends. That is the failure mode 3.1 names — not the GM gifting items, but a permanent frictionless market. Recommendation: change — give the village market a supply constraint rather than a risk one. The wares cap and the clock-based restock already exist (below); lean on them rather than treating the village as an unlimited counter. A concrete test: run twenty village turns with 5,000 gp and measure whether the hero can leave arbitrarily equipped.

B. The wares mechanism will not carry "sell your inventory here" — grounded in code. Positions: 3.1 ●, 5.3 ● (uniformity: divergence past a point stops being the same game). fileWare (memory.js:326) files onto _waresWorldNode (memory.js:318), which keys off worldState.world.location only — the settlement node, never the sub-location. Every shop in the village writes to one shared list. That list is capped by settlement size (waresCapFor, WARES_CAP_BY_SIZE = {small:2, medium:4, large:6…}, globals.js:78) and overflow is dropped with node.wares.shift() and a console.warn. Meanwhile fileLocationItem (memory.js:393) does key off currentNodeKey(), which includes the sublocation — so houses are correctly separate. The asymmetry means: items left in a house persist per-house; items sold at the blacksmith land in one village-wide pile of 2–6 that silently evicts the oldest. A player who sells eight items and returns for one will find it gone, with nothing said — which also collides with the project's own no-silent-failures rule. Recommendation: change — either scope wares to the sub-location the way location items already are, or state in the design that shop-sold goods are lossy and surface the eviction to the player. Do not ship the current asymmetry unexamined.

D. Residents as playable characters is the strongest part of the proposal. Positions: 3.4 ● (henchmen "usually spell the difference between failure and success", and let play continue without the main PC), 7.2 ◐ (places with inhabitants that persist). Routing "which character do I play" through _switchPlayerCharacter (ui-sheets.js:663) reuses a path that already demotes the old hero to a full NPC with their sheet, migrates relationships and clears activePC. Group 1 — Computational stylometry — what measurably distinguishes authors  medium confidence
Hypothesis
Authorial identity is carried mainly by high-frequency, low-salience DISTRIBUTIONAL features — function-word rates, character n-grams, punctuation rates, sentence-length mean AND variance — which are precisely the features a prose directive cannot specify and a generator will not follow as an instruction. A name works because it retrieves a stored joint distribution over those features; a 12-dial list fails because it asks the model to satisfy twelve salient descriptions simultaneously and it averages them instead. Therefore a name-free directive succeeds exactly to the degree that it does two things: (a) names a retrievable POPULATION (usually a genre) whose distributional centroid sits near the target author — which is why Lovecraft/Poe landed and Muir did not; and (b) converts the residue that no population retrieves into explicitly COUNTABLE mechanical constraints (words per sentence and its spread, comma/dash/semicolon rates, fragment count, literal repetition counts) rather than adjectives. Corollary and the sharpest prediction: the Lovecraft-fantastic / Poe-fine gap is not about lexical-vs-rhythmic being intrinsically unspecifiable, it is that Lovecraft's markers were already stated as retrievable lexical categories while Poe's were stated as adjectives ("mounting cadence", "musical") — restate Poe's cadence as numbers and the gap closes.
Key evidence
  • Function-word frequency is called 'the single most reliable indicator of authorship' independently in all five briefs, and is described as used UNCONSCIOUSLY and topic-independently (Stamatatos survey; Programming Historian 'Introduction to stylometry with Python'; MDPI Authorship Attribution survey). These are exactly the features no style directive ever mentions and no author could self-report.
  • Mosteller & Wallace (1964, Federalist Papers, via toolingup.stanford.edu): 30 'marker' function words separated Hamilton from Madison; Hamilton used 'upon' roughly 10x more often than Madison. The discriminating signal was a preposition rate, not imagery, diction, or tone.
  • Burrows' Delta (2002) operates on the 200-300 most frequent words (overwhelmingly function words): 92.6% correct attribution on single-authored Early Modern English plays, 95.7% on highest-confidence subset; Cosine Delta outperforms it (90%+ adjusted Rand index); >90% typical accuracy across implementations (Briefs 1 and 5). Critically for us, Brief 1 reports Delta holding 80%+ on texts of only 100-550 words — the size of our lab rewrites.
  • JGAAP (Java Graphical Authorship Attribution Program) using this feature family identified J.K. Rowling behind 'The Cuckoo's Calling' (Brief 5). A book-length voice deliberately disguised by its own author was still caught by distributional features — evidence that these features are both decisive and outside conscious control.
  • Character n-grams (n=3-8) reach >=90% accuracy and are explicitly 'robust to topic shift' (Brief 5, N-gram feature selection / character n-gram robustness studies). But the same brief reports word vs character n-gram performance is statistically equivalent (mean 77.90 vs 80.89) — so 'character n-grams dominate' is overstated; the honest reading is that several unconscious surface-statistic families all work.
  • Syntactic features alone hit >77% accuracy across 26 authors (Influence of Lexical, Syntactic and Structural Features, ScienceDirect), and syntactic features are described as 'deep linguistic features comparatively more difficult to consciously manipulate'. POS n-grams underperform lexical/character features because the tag inventory is only ~50-100 items versus thousands of lexical items (Briefs 1 and 2).
  • Sentence length: weak as a standalone feature but contributes meaningfully in multi-feature models, and the VARIANCE/distribution shape carries signal distinct from the mean (Brief 2). Brief 2's explicit NEGATIVE finding: no published threshold ranges define what 'short', 'medium' or 'long' means for prose authors — our 1-10 Cadence dial has no external calibration whatsoever.
  • Punctuation is 'a largely overlooked stylistic feature' yet author-distinctive; tracked as comma rate per 100 tokens, em-/en-dash rate, semicolon preference, exclamation rate; and syntactically CLASSIFIED punctuation beats raw mark counts (Cambridge, 'Pull out all the stops: Textual analysis via punctuation sequences'). No brief could rank which mark is most diagnostic.
  • Style-vs-genre overlap, quantified (Brief 5, arXiv 2411.04950): stop words make up 26.5% of author-distinctive tokens versus 23.7% of genre-distinctive tokens, pronouns the most common type at 11.5-12.96%. Author signal and genre signal live in nearly the SAME feature space — direct mechanistic support for Hypothesis 2 (a genre name is a near-equivalent pointer), and simultaneously its ceiling (genre retrieves a population centroid, not an individual).
  • Cross-genre attribution accuracy drops to 77.27% versus single-genre, and models 'conflate author identity with topic and genre rather than learning genuine stylistic patterns' (Separating Style from Substance, arXiv 2408.05192; CROSSNEWS). Hard-positive plus hard-negative sample selection produced a 62.7% relative improvement in cross-genre attribution — i.e. the field's own fix for genre/author entanglement is contrastive pressure, the generation-side analogue of which is 'two voices that share a genre must be differentiated on something other than the genre handle'.
  • Rhythm/cadence is a consistent NEGATIVE finding in four of five briefs: no dedicated prose-rhythm feature research surfaced; rhythm work is siloed in verse (syllabic-quantity features for Latin, assonance/consonance useful only inside ensembles, accentual regularity acting as an 'inhibiting factor'); Brief 5 states no competition result isolates rhythm as a baseline against lexical methods. The literature has no operational vocabulary for prose rhythm — which is the same handicap our Poe directive has.
  • Vocabulary-richness measures are a dead end as levers: TTR is length-sensitive, VOCD values decline as text length grows, richness metrics show 'extreme variability in large text groups' and are 'of marginal value in large-scale stylistic studies', and are explicitly weaker for GENRE differentiation than for authorship (Briefs 4 and 5). Only MTLD/MATTR/HD-D are length-stable.
  • Brief 3's decisive negative: 'No published work specifically measures how genre-neutral prose DESCRIPTIONS (vs dial lists vs named author references) perform as re-identification vectors.' The exact experiment this project is running has no prior art — no literature will adjudicate Hypothesis 2 for us.
Implications for shipping
  • Stop judging arms by ear alone — add a pure-JS measurement harness to author_voice_lab.html that scores every output on the feature families the field says actually discriminate: a Burrows'/Cosine Delta over the top 200-300 most frequent words, punctuation rates per 100 tokens (comma, dash, semicolon, exclamation), sentence-length mean AND standard deviation, and fragment rate. Use the AUTHOR-NAME CONTROL arm's output as the target centroid (no author corpus needed, no API cost). Delta holds 80%+ at 100-550 words, so pool 3-5 rewrites per arm before trusting a distance. This converts 'fantastic vs fine' into a number and would have caught the dial-averaging failure (Ornament 9 + Grandeur 9 drowning Humor 8) mechanically.
  • Rewrite the rhythm-bearing clauses of every distilled directive as COUNTABLE constraints instead of adjectives, and run Poe as the discriminating case. 'Build unease through repetition and mounting cadence' and 'musical and deliberate' specify nothing measurable; the replacement is explicit: mean sentence ~28 words with a 6-45 spread, at least one phrase repeated verbatim three times with each recurrence shorter than the last, semicolons present, comma rate ~2.5 per sentence. Prediction: Poe moves toward Lovecraft's result and its Delta distance to the name-control shrinks. If it does NOT, the lexical-vs-rhythmic sub-finding is real and rhythm is genuinely un-promptable — which would be a novel finding, since the literature has no answer either.
  • Treat a genre handle as retrieval of a POPULATION CENTROID, and rank voices by how close the author sits to that centroid. This predicts a testable ordering: voices who effectively ARE their genre's centroid (Lovecraft/cosmic horror, Poe/gothic, Howard/sword-and-sorcery, Rice/vampire gothic, Abnett/military SF, Moorcock/doomed-albino high fantasy) ship on a short directive; outliers INSIDE a shared genre (Le Guin, Gaiman, Clines) will land generically — recognizable as the genre, not as the voice; genre-less voices (Muir, Wells, Dinniman) need the most authoring. On the planned Wells-vs-Rice discriminator, log a third prediction that Hypothesis 1 and 2 both miss: Rice lands but generically, because the handle retrieves the genre centroid rather than the individual.
  • For the genre-less voices, build a SYNTHETIC handle by INTERSECTING two retrievable populations plus a switching rule, rather than by averaging dials or writing longer descriptions. Muir = 'gothic funerary ritual' x 'modern group-chat banter', alternating within the paragraph; Wells = 'workplace-competence procedural' x 'anxious first-person interior monologue'; Dinniman = 'livestream/speedrun commentary' x 'body-horror dungeon crawl'. Each pointer retrieves a coherent joint distribution the way a name does; the collision IS the voice. This directly attacks the diagnosed failure mode (averaging) with the mechanism the evidence says works (retrieval).
  • Keep the 12 dials strictly as the authoring UI that generates a distilled paragraph, and never ship a raw dial list into buildSysPrompt. The evidence explains why they lose: dials name the salient, consciously-controllable minority of style (imagery, diction, tone) while the discriminating mass is unconscious distributional statistics; and 12 simultaneous extreme scalars are a constraint-satisfaction problem the model resolves by averaging. Also drop vocabulary-richness ideas (TTR, hapax ratio, Yule's K) from both the dial space and any metric — they are length-sensitive, genre-confounded, and of marginal value at scale.
  • Adopt 'unmasking' as a cheap per-clause diagnostic before the shipping rewrite: ablate one clause at a time from each distilled directive, regenerate, and measure the Delta shift against the name-control centroid. Clauses whose removal moves nothing are prompt-token waste; the one or two whose removal collapses the distance are the real carriers, and those are what a shared signature-device registry (already scoped in TODO #104) should be built from.
What the evidence could not answer
  • The bridge assumption is untested and the briefs cannot test it: stylometry measures what a CLASSIFIER uses to attribute finished text (function-word rates, character n-grams), while our ear tests measure what a READER perceives as voice (imagery, jokes, diction weirdness). These may be different feature sets. If they are, matching a Delta distance could be satisfied by prose that still reads wrong, and vice versa — the harness must be validated against a handful of by-ear verdicts before it is trusted as an arbiter.
  • Every source is about DETECTION, none about INDUCTION. No brief contains a single result on whether describing a feature to a generator produces that feature. The entire generation side of the project's question is unstudied (Brief 3 states this explicitly for prose descriptions as re-identification vectors).
  • No ablation study anywhere ranks single feature types (lexical vs syntactic vs semantic vs rhythmic vs prosodic) with topic and genre held constant — Brief 5 flags this as an explicit gap. So the briefs cannot tell us whether the Lovecraft/Poe difference is a lexical-vs-rhythmic effect at all, or an artifact of directive wording.
  • No published thresholds define short/medium/long sentence-length signatures for prose authors (Brief 2 negative). Our 1-10 dial bands are therefore uncalibrated inventions; converting them to numbers requires measuring our own reference passages, not consulting the literature.
  • Prose rhythm has essentially no operational feature vocabulary — rhythm research is siloed in verse (syllabic quantity, accentual regularity), and no competition isolates it. Whatever cadence metric the harness uses will have to be invented in-house (sentence-length autocorrelation, clause-length series, repetition counts) with no external validation.
  • Nothing quantifies how far a genre centroid sits from an individual author inside that genre, so the centroid-proximity ranking above is a prediction with no prior measurement behind it. Related: no work compares author-signal portability across dramatically different genres at scale (the largest cross-genre benchmark, CROSSNEWS, covers only news and social media).
  • No comparative ranking exists of which punctuation mark (comma vs semicolon vs dash) is individually most diagnostic, so the harness must weight them empirically rather than by prior.
  • Minimum reliable sample size for our specific case is unresolved: Delta's 80%+ at 100-550 words comes from an AI-detection study on essays, not from short stylized fiction rewrites, so the pooling requirement per arm is a guess that the harness should itself measure (run the same arm twice and check the self-distance floor).

Group 8 — Specifying rhythm — the lexical-vs-rhythmic gap  medium confidence
Hypothesis
Rhythm is not intrinsically less promptable than diction — it fails when it is written as a FELT QUALITY the model must average ("mounting cadence", Cadence=9) instead of as an ORTHOGRAPHIC OPERATION the model can literally emit. Claim: a name-free directive reproduces a voice's rhythm at diction-level fidelity if and only if its rhythm clauses name countable, orthographically-realized operations — sentence-length targets and long/short alternation, punctuation marks (em-dash caesura, comma/semicolon density), repeated clause openers, and named rhetorical schemes (anaphora, epistrophe, tricolon, polysyndeton, asyndeton, periodic vs loose) — because those are things in the token stream. Rhythm features with NO orthographic realization (stress pattern, syllable count, isochrony, sibilance/assonance) are unreachable through any prompt, which imposes a hard per-voice ceiling proportional to how much of that voice's music lives below the token layer. Corollary for the live Hypothesis 2: "genre handle" is a special case of a more general rule — a directive works when every clause is a POINTER at something retrievable (a genre, a named rhetorical scheme, a countable form constraint) and fails when a clause is a scalar description to be averaged. Poe came out merely "fine" not because rhythm is unspecifiable but because his distilled paragraph specifies rhythm adjectivally while Lovecraft's specifies diction concretely.
Key evidence
  • Architecture, the load-bearing mechanism (Brief 2): subword tokenization gives the model no native syllable-segmentation layer, so syllable/stress constraints are learned approximations while vocabulary is directly tokenized. This predicts exactly which rhythm features are promptable — the ones with orthographic realization — and is the only well-established (non-anecdotal) fact in the five briefs.
  • Compliance asymmetry, directional only (Brief 2, community consensus, NOT peer-reviewed): lexical/vocabulary constraints ~85–95% adherence; syllable constraints rarely above 70%; explicit sentence-length caps ("under 12 words") ~70–80% and DEGRADING with output length; abstract structural instructions ("use parallel structure in every sentence") yield ~1–3 instances in an 8-sentence response, i.e. token gestures rather than systematic adherence.
  • Brief 2 independently corroborates Hypothesis 2 without knowing about it: "named literary genre constraints (gothic horror, noir detective) are more reliably followed than abstract rhythm descriptors — genre-as-proxy is a documented prompt-engineering technique."
  • Brief 2's own summary states the project's sub-finding in reverse: "cadence cannot be reliably specified without vocabulary anchoring — 'energetic, punchy prose' works better than 'vary sentence length from 4 to 25 words' alone; rhythm appears downstream of lexical choice." This is the one item that CUTS AGAINST the hypothesis and must be tested head-on (see gaps).
  • Brief 5: repetition schemes are the promptable half of rhythm — anaphora (n-gram prefix match), epistrophe (suffix match), polysyndeton (conjunction ratio), tricolon (3 parallel units) are all countable and pedagogically "checkable"; explicit "start 3 consecutive sentences with the same word" outperforms "write in iambic pentameter" (Brief 2, poetry-generation case studies). Brief 5's explicit caveat: the leap from "use anaphora" to "achieves Poe-like rhythm" is NOT bridged in any published work.
  • Brief 4's Poe inventory splits cleanly along the orthographic line: repetition/anaphora/epistrophe (orthographic ✓), em-dash and comma caesura fragmenting sentences into "pieces of sound" (✓), accumulation in a short-long-long-LONG crescendo (✓), sibilant/plosive clustering and "phonetic rhythm" (✗, sub-token), suspected isochrony (✗, and Brief 4 reports NO acoustic study exists). Roughly three of five of Poe's rhythm devices are recoverable; the phonetic layer is not — a precise explanation for "fine, not fantastic" and a predicted ceiling below Lovecraft's even after a fix.
  • Brief 4 cross-author typology gives a free difficulty ranking: McCarthy = parataxis/asyndeton/functional-word repetition, Hemingway = short declarative baseline with minimal subordination, Stein = anaphoric loop + gerundive continuity — all three are purely syntactic/orthographic and should be highly promptable; Poe alone is phonetic/musical. Mapped onto our roster, the clipped voices (Abercrombie, Cook, Abnett, Clines, Wells, Dinniman) are rhythmically EASY; the musical high-Cadence/high-Ornament voices (Poe, Rice, Moorcock, Muir) are the hard column.
  • Brief 3, decisive negative: no prose-rhythm notation exists anywhere. Musical notation has no prose beat grid; poetic scansion's binary feet were abandoned for prose; IPA stress marks and ToBI (Silverman et al. 1992) never left phonetics; SSML controls synthesis, not description. Literary criticism has only phenomenological labels — "periodic", "loose", "staccato", "flowing", "run-on". So there is no notation to borrow: any rhythm vocabulary we ship, we invent.
  • Brief 1, the proxy-metric shortlist that IS available: average sentence length (Hemingway 12–15 words vs James 40+), sentence-length variance, clause depth (parataxis vs hypotaxis), punctuation density per 1000 words, em-dash frequency as author signature (Le Guin high, Hemingway near-zero), lexical density, type-token ratio.
  • Brief 1, second decisive negative: no computational framework isolates rhythm from vocabulary and syntax; Burrows' Delta / Mosteller & Wallace measure an authorship fingerprint, not rhythm; Stanford Literary Lab treats rhythm as secondary. Rhythm in published stylometry is "emergent from vocabulary + syntax + punctuation" — which means our numbers can only ever be a proxy, never the verdict.
  • Apparent contradiction, resolved: Brief 1 says punctuation and em-dash patterns are strong measurable author signatures; Brief 2 says structural patterns are weakly constrained by prompt. Both hold — measurable ≠ promptable — and the resolution is the actionable lever: punctuation marks and sentence boundaries ARE literal tokens, so they are the most promptable rhythm surface available, while stress and syllables are not tokens at all.
  • Blanket source caveat: ALL FIVE briefs exhausted their web budget and report from Feb-2025 training knowledge. Brief 2 states outright that no formal study comparing lexical vs rhythmic constraint adherence exists in ACL/EMNLP/ICLR 2023–2025; Briefs 1, 3, 4 and 5 each log their own equivalent negative. The percentages above are community estimates, not measurements, and should never be cited as evidence in DOC_author_voice.md.
Implications for shipping
  • Change the FORM of rhythm clauses, not their amount. In VOICE_DISTILLED, rewrite adjectival rhythm language into countable orthographic ops. Poe's "Build unease through repetition and mounting cadence… long sentences welcome but musical" becomes e.g. "Repeat a key phrase three times across the passage, each return tighter. Break long sentences with em-dashes mid-clause. Follow the longest sentence immediately with one under six words." Same length, same no-name guard, ops instead of adjectives — this is the cheapest discriminating experiment available and it isolates specification-FORM with genre held constant (both arms are gothic).
  • Run the reverse ablation on Lovecraft in the same session: keep his rhythm clauses, replace his concrete diction spec ("formal, antiquarian, scholarly and slightly archaic", "one archaic weird adjective per beat") with scalar equivalents ("high ornament, high formality"). If he drops from fantastic, the variable is specification-form, not modality, and the lexical-vs-rhythmic framing is retired in favour of pointer-vs-description.
  • Add a rhythm-op REGISTRY as Layer 2's sibling — one shared name-free table of countable devices (anaphora, epistrophe, tricolon, polysyndeton, asyndeton, fragment-after-long, em-dash caesura, periodic vs loose sentence, short/long alternation) that voices reference by entry, exactly the registry shape already planned for the signature-device dropdown in TODO #104. Adding a device is an entry, not per-author prose. Concretely this means the Cadence dial can no longer emit band text alone: the dial→directive generator must resolve a Cadence value to ops.
  • Instrument the lab with a numeric ear-proxy per arm — mean sentence length, sentence-length coefficient of variation, longest:shortest ratio, punctuation density per 100 words, repeated-opener count — shown beside the same numbers computed on that voice's flavor reference. The prediction that makes it worth building: the dial/adjectival arm regresses toward a house mean (mid-length, low variance) regardless of the Cadence rating, which is finding #1's "averaging" made visible instead of arguable. Keep it a proxy — per project rule the ear is ground truth (Brief 1: no metric isolates rhythm).
  • Abandon any attempt to specify SOUND. No stress patterns, no iambic-leaning cadence, no alliteration or sibilance targets: the model has no syllable layer (Brief 2), no notation exists (Brief 3), and metrical analysis of prose was abandoned (Briefs 1 and 3 agree). Spend those directive tokens on diction instead — for phonetically-driven voices, compensate with the 85–95%-compliant lever: specify the vocabulary OF dread rather than its music, and accept a lower ceiling for Poe than for Lovecraft.
  • Rank the shipping backlog on TWO independent axes, not one. Hypothesis 2's hard list (no genre handle: Muir, Wells, Dinniman, Gaiman, Clines) and the rhythm-hard list (high-Cadence musical voices: Poe, Rice, Moorcock, Muir) are different lists; a voice on both is the worst case — which is exactly Muir (Cadence 9, Ornament 9, no genre name), matching the field result that Muir needed the most scaffolding. Run the planned Wells-vs-Rice discriminator, but add the Poe rhythm-op rerun as the second discriminator.
  • Test compliance DECAY inside one turn before shipping. Sentence-length adherence degrades with output length (Brief 2), and game narration runs 150–250 words inside a large system prompt. Measure op compliance in the first vs last third of a generated turn; if it decays, the fix is positional — STYLE already sits at the very end of the volatile half (§6, load-bearing per audit #2), which is the right place to restate the op rule.
What the evidence could not answer
  • No published study anywhere compares lexical vs rhythmic constraint adherence in LLMs (Brief 2 checked ACL/EMNLP/ICLR 2023–2025 and found none). Every compliance number in this synthesis (85–95%, ~70%, 70–80%, 1–3 of 8) is community/forum consensus repeated from training knowledge, not measurement. The asymmetry itself is only anecdotally established; only the tokenization explanation is solid.
  • All five agents exhausted their web budget and retrieved ZERO live sources; everything is pre-Feb-2025 recall. Named sources are canonical (Flesch 1948, Mosteller & Wallace, Silverman et al. 1992 ToBI, Lanham's Handlist, Silva Rhetoricae) but the specific claims attached to them are mostly reported as "general knowledge, no named study".
  • Directly contradicting evidence left unresolved: Brief 2 asserts rhythm is DOWNSTREAM of lexical choice and that vocabulary-anchored phrasing ("punchy prose") beats explicit numeric length rules. If true, the countable-op hypothesis is wrong in the specific case of sentence-length numerics and the fix is richer diction, not more ops. The Poe A/B must therefore test three arms — adjectival (current), countable-op, and vocabulary-anchored — or it cannot distinguish these.
  • No evidence at all on whether the model can be told to hit a rhythm TARGET it can't perceive in its own output: the briefs never establish that an LLM can self-check sentence-length variance or anaphora placement while generating. Compliance may be a generation-time accident rather than a followed instruction.
  • Nothing on durability. Every observation is a single-passage rewrite; the game runs hundreds of turns. A "repeat an opener three times per passage" rule that reads as Poe once may read as a tic by turn 40. Repetition fatigue over a long run is unmeasured and needs the /playtest corpus, not the lab.
  • Nothing on how any of this survives the real prompt environment — a large cached stable half, second-person present tense, state-tag emission, and suggestion-call interaction. All lab evidence is a clean isolated rewrite task; transfer to buildSysPrompt is assumed, not shown.
  • No source bridges rhetorical scheme → perceived author rhythm (Brief 5 states this explicitly), and no cross-author rhythm comparison using standardized metrics exists (Brief 1). So the proxy metrics have no published thresholds — we can only compare an arm against our own flavor reference, never against a validated target.
  • Brief 4's author profiles are secondary literary criticism with several explicit holes (no research on Poe's SYNTAX-level rhythm, no acoustic measurement of his musicality, no framework unifying the four authors). The Poe device inventory used to predict his ceiling is therefore critic-derived and partly speculative.

Group 9 — Human imitation craft — parody, pastiche, ghostwriting  medium confidence
Hypothesis
A name-free directive succeeds exactly to the degree it uses the two channels prose description can actually carry — (a) a CORPUS-ADDRESSABLE HANDLE (a genre, document-type, register, or narrator-archetype label that resolves to a dense region the model already represents) and (b) LEXICON + PROCEDURAL CONSTRAINTS (which words, and what the narrator must say, withhold, or reveal in what order) — and it plateaus on RHYTHM, because no human imitation tradition (parody, ghostwriting, fan fiction, MFA pedagogy, forensic stylometry) has ever produced a prescriptive vocabulary for cadence; every tradition transmits rhythm by EXEMPLAR (copywork / the Franklin method) instead. Testable prediction: diction-led and constraint-led voices (Lovecraft, Cook, Wells, Clines, Abnett) will land under description alone; rhythm-led voices (Poe, Rice, Le Guin, Moorcock, and Muir's ornate-but-complete sentences) will stay at "fine" under ANY purely descriptive directive and will only close the gap when given a name-free exemplar passage or a quantified prosodic spec (sentence-length distribution, fragment ratio, punctuation ratios) in place of a "Cadence 7" dial.
Key evidence
  • Four of five briefs independently rank DICTION first in the imitation hierarchy: parody practice (Brief 1, MAD Magazine methodology — vocabulary catalogs before syntax), fan communities (Brief 3, verbatim consensus phrasing "word choice is portable, rhythm is intuitive"), ghostwriting (Brief 2, Ludlum/Bourne continuations used a studied per-character word-choice inventory; anachronistic diction forbidden), and MFA craft texts (Brief 4, Prose, Reading Like a Writer, 2006; Lamott, Bird by Bird, 1994).
  • Rhythm is universally named as load-bearing and universally reported as un-teachable by description. Brief 3: "Pacing is the hardest to fake; you learn it by osmosis, not instruction." Brief 1 records an explicit absence — literary criticism discusses cadence qualitatively but offers "no systematic vocabulary for encoding RHYTHMIC patterns into prompts separate from diction." Brief 4 flags the lexical-vs-rhythmic transfer comparison as a gap in cognitive linguistics.
  • The one human method that DOES transmit rhythm is exemplar-based, not descriptive: Franklin's three-stage method (read passage, set aside, rewrite from memory, compare) explicitly targets sentence structure and grammatical arrangement, not vocabulary or subject; copywork (Goldberg, Writing Down the Bones, 1986) is described as motor-memory internalization of rhythm and punctuation. Neither is a description channel.
  • Brief 5 appears to contradict the diction-first ranking — stylometry finds lexical/function-word markers are the HARDEST to forge, while "surface features (sentence rhythm, metaphor frequency, plot structure) are easier to copy" (Argamon & Jurafsky; Jockers & Witten, Macroanalysis; Mosteller & Wallace's Federalist function-word method). The contradiction dissolves on the agent: a human forger cannot suppress an unconscious idiolect, so lexis betrays them; an LLM has no idiolect to leak and executes an explicit lexical instruction directly. For our case the two findings AGREE that lexis is the reliably specifiable layer and rhythm is the unconscious/absorbed one.
  • Genre-as-voice-carrier is corroborated in two independent domains: Brief 1 (postmodern parody clusters authors inside recognizable genres — gothic, noir, comedic-grotesque — that carry markers without the author name; Lovecraft/Poe align with "cosmic horror"/"psychological gothic" which pre-exist the author) and Brief 2 (Tom Clancy continuations stabilize house voice through "military procedural accuracy" rather than prose imitation; hard-boiled and space-opera continuations do the same).
  • The strongest COUNTER-datum to a naive Hypothesis 2 comes from Brief 3 (Reddit r/FanFiction, 2024): "Pratchett's voice is 'fantasy comedy' but that's reductive — lots of funny fantasy authors sound nothing like Pratchett." Genre is a real pointer but a LOW-RESOLUTION one; it needs a disambiguator layered on top, which is precisely the role our Layer-2 signature devices play.
  • Brief 2's cross-franchise consensus is "voice is pattern, not prose": readers detect violations of structural/decision-rule patterns (what gets revealed and when, pacing, chapter rhythm, which characters die) faster than sentence-level style drift. Fleming estate continuations reportedly ship a "tone checklist" plus approved frameworks and forbidden scenarios; the Clancy trust shipped a narrative bible. All are constraint lists, not attribute vectors.
  • Our own shipped VOICE_DISTILLED paragraphs (author_voice_lab.html lines 229-244) already encode both winning channels, which is a plausible mechanism for why that arm beat the dials: procedural constraints the 12-dial model has NO slot for (clines "reveal the strange one piece at a time"; wells "convey feeling only through observation and understatement, never by naming the emotion"; lovecraft "describe by implication"; gaiman "at most one metaphor per scene") and corpus handles (lovecraft "Cosmic dread", poe "Gothic, macabre", abnett "a war report written by someone with excellent nerves", gaiman "a bedtime story that knows something it isn't telling you", cook "tired-soldier narration").
  • Brief 1 proposes the concrete substitute for a missing genre: authorial STANCE (earnestness vs irony, intimacy vs distance, complicity vs judgment) plus social register/dialect (Gass on narrative voice) as a corpus-recognizable anchor — naming Gaiman/Clines as ironic-distance-with-emotional-permission and Wells (Murderbot) as deadpan sincerity, i.e. exactly our five genre-less cases.
  • Brief 1's stated hierarchy is Diction → Syntax → Tone(register+irony) → Figuration, with figuration explicitly TERTIARY and emerging only after diction and rhythm are set. Our 12 dials are flat and co-equal, which is a plausible mechanism for finding 1's "extreme dials drown each other" (Ornament 9 + Grandeur 9 swamping Humor 8) — no craft tradition treats these as a flat vector.
  • Four explicit NEGATIVE findings converge: no published methodology for assigning a synthetic genre handle to an idiosyncratic author (Brief 1); no continuation author has published a quantified attribute system (Brief 2); no fan-studies or academic work on removing author identity while preserving voice (Brief 3, having scanned Fan Studies Review and Transformative Works and Cultures); no forgery research on synthesizing style FROM description rather than FROM a corpus (Brief 5). The project is in genuinely uncharted territory — nobody has solved this and no literature will hand us the answer.
  • Brief 5's success cases are irrelevant as method but relevant as ship-safety framing: King/Bachman, Ferrante, and Rowling/Galbraith held via secrecy, not stylistic imperceptibility (Galbraith broke in three months via a Times source, with no linguistic detection preceding it), and stylometric attribution's ~90% accuracy requires substantial text. Accepted pastiche mimics surface features WITHOUT claiming authorship — which is exactly the shape a de-branded prose voice takes.
Implications for shipping
  • Promote the corpus handle to a required FIELD, not an accident of prose. Every voice gets one explicit handle phrase: a genre name where one exists (lovecraft "cosmic horror", poe "psychological gothic", howard "sword-and-sorcery", muir "gothic"), else a document-type / narrator-archetype / register phrase (abnett already has "a war report written by someone with excellent nerves"; cook "tired-soldier narration"; gaiman "a bedtime story that knows something it isn't telling you"). The falsification test is cheap and symmetric in the existing lab: DELETE the handle clause from lovecraft/poe (predict degradation) and ADD a synthetic handle to the five genre-less voices — muir, wells, dinniman, gaiman, clines (predict improvement). If neither moves, Hypothesis 2 is wrong and the handle is decoration.
  • Reframe Hypothesis 2: the working ingredient is not "genre" but POINTER + DISAMBIGUATOR. Genre is one kind of low-resolution pointer (the Pratchett/"fantasy comedy" objection is fatal to genre alone), and Layer-2 signature devices are the disambiguator that narrows inside the pointed-at region. This predicts the observed spread: Lovecraft needed the least scaffolding because the handle is high-resolution; Muir needed the most because no handle existed to narrow from.
  • Add a real third layer for PROCEDURAL CONSTRAINTS — what the narrator must withhold, reveal, or refuse — because "voice is pattern, not prose" says that's what readers catch first and the 12 scalar dials have no slot for it. Harvest the ones already smuggled into VOICE_DISTILLED ("never name the emotion", "describe by implication", "one piece at a time", "at most one metaphor per scene", "undercut every dramatic beat") into an explicit list. These are also the most enforceable clauses in a game-GM prompt, since they are rules rather than aesthetics.
  • For rhythm-led voices, switch channels from description to EXEMPLAR — the Franklin/copywork channel, the only one any tradition uses for cadence. This costs nothing new: author_voice_lab.html already holds VOICE_FLAVOR (lines 250-265), hand-written author-free passages of the same cellar scene per voice. Add a fourth lab arm that ships DISTILLED + the flavor passage as "match the rhythm and sentence shapes of this sample, not its content", and test it on poe / rice / leguin / moorcock. If Poe jumps from "fine" to "fantastic" while Lovecraft (already fantastic on diction alone) barely moves, the lexical-vs-rhythmic sub-finding is confirmed with a mechanism and a fix.
  • Alternative rhythm channel worth one arm: replace the Cadence/Momentum dials with QUANTIFIED prosody borrowed from stylometry's actual variables — target mean sentence length, sentence-length variance, fragment ratio, clause-nesting depth, punctuation ratios (em-dash/semicolon/comma). "Most sentences under twelve words" (already in the abercrombie distilled) is the one rhythm instruction in our set that is executable rather than evocative, and it is the abercrombie voice's strongest marker. Numbers are the closest thing to a prescriptive rhythm vocabulary that exists.
  • Fix the dial-drowning by ordering rather than by re-rating. Emit the 12 attributes in the craft hierarchy Diction → Syntax → Tone/Stance → Figuration with an explicit precedence sentence ("where these conflict, the earlier wins"), instead of as a flat co-equal list. No tradition treats them as a vector to average, and a stated precedence gives the model a tie-break rule for the Ornament-9-vs-Humor-8 collision instead of forcing it to blend.
What the evidence could not answer
  • Zero live citations. All five briefs exhausted their web budget and report from training knowledge, so nothing here is a verified source — including the specific claims (MAD's vocabulary-catalog methodology, the Fleming estate "tone checklist", the Clancy narrative bible, Van Lustbader's rereading regimen, the r/FanFiction Pratchett quote). Treat named sources as leads to verify, not as evidence. The Brief 5 item on "John Bowe's collection of Flannery O'Connor letters" looks confabulated and I have discarded it.
  • The five briefs are not five independent witnesses — same model, overlapping training data — so their convergence on diction-first is weaker evidence than five independent domains would be. It is consistent with the possibility that one popular craft framing is being echoed five times.
  • No brief could quantify anything about rhythm: no target sentence-length distributions, no punctuation ratios, no fragment rates for any author. The quantified-prosody implication is a proposal derived from stylometry's variable list, not a recipe any source supplied.
  • No source addresses the model-side question at all — attribute averaging/interference, pointer-vs-description, or how an LLM resolves a style description. Brief 3 explicitly reports fan communities have no concept of it. Our own lab remains the only evidence on finding 1.
  • Nobody has published a method for synthesizing a genre handle for a genre-less author (Brief 1's explicit negative). The stance/register substitute (irony vs earnestness, deadpan sincerity, social register) is Brief 1's inference, not a documented technique, and it has never been tested against a name control by anyone.
  • The briefs cannot tell us whether a handle works because it names a genre or merely because it is any label with dense corpus support — the distinction our reframing turns on. Only the strip/add experiment in the lab can separate those.
  • No evidence on durability: whether a name-free directive holds voice over a long GM run the way a name does, which is the actual shipping question for a campaign spanning hundreds of turns. Everything in these briefs concerns single-passage imitation.

Finding 4 · Inventory size and missing item canon

Validity. The schema point is valid: the active inventory is plain strings and the engine has no canonical effect record for mechanics-bearing items. The quantitative premise does not reproduce. A fresh t1549 prompt build produced 35,870 stable characters and 67,597 volatile characters. Ammut's complete 107-item Inventory: line is 5,027 characters, or about 1,257 tokens under the report's own characters/4 estimator—not 2,691. STORY SO FAR (~1,952) and ACTIVE NPC DETAILS (~1,790) are therefore larger. Companion inventories together add about 683 estimated tokens inside their separate party blocks, but that still does not make the claimed “one line” measurement true. With no field contradiction demonstrated, this is useful evidence for existing #81, not a new moderate-priority incident.

• Structured inventory should compress the prompt, never the saved possessions. Auto-categorizing 107 legacy strings is itself an error surface, and collapsing trophies or “mundane” objects into a count can erase the clue that later becomes plot-relevant. Preserve every item structurally; inject full names for quest/provenance/mechanics-bearing items and summarize only a reversible presentation view. “Available on demand via the sheet” does not help the GM during a generation unless an actual retrieval/tool path exists.
